results.title: Launch YC: Pluto - AI voice agent that helps professionals get discovered | Y Combinator
results.content:
A resume and online profile are not enough for the AI era.

They show where someone worked and what title they had. They do not capture what the person actually did, what they are unusually good at, and what they want next.

That context usually lives in conversations. So professionals get reduced to keywords, logos, and titles, while the people and AI agents trying to understand them are left with an incomplete picture.

Hiring makes this problem obvious. Companies miss great people because the real signal never makes it online. But as AI agents increasingly help people find, evaluate, and connect with one another, every professional will need a richer, more accurate way to be understood.

### The solution [...] TL;DR - A professional talks to Pluto for 10 minutes about what they’ve done, what they’re great at, and what they want next. Pluto makes that context discoverable to the right people and AI agents, helping them understand the person more fully. When there’s a real fit, Pluto can also make a warm introduction to a startup.

18K+ professionals have already shared their career context with Pluto. 100+ companies use Pluto to meet people with their full story, including Mercor, David AI, Rho, Warp, and Runlayer.

Ask: Talk to Pluto and let it get to know your work. If you’re hiring, send us the role and we’ll introduce you to people with context and confirmed interest.

### The problem

A resume and online profile are not enough for the AI era. [...] ### The solution

Pluto is an AI voice agent that understands a professional’s career and puts that understanding to work.

Professionals talk to Pluto for 10 minutes about their experience, strengths, goals, preferences, and what they want to keep private. Pluto asks follow-up questions, remembers the context missing from their resume, and makes them discoverable to the right people and AI agents.

Companies tell Pluto who they want to meet. Pluto searches its network and the broader market, understands fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and makes a warm introduction when both sides want to connect. No mass applications. Professionals stay private and in control. Companies meet people who are already understood.

How It Works

Congrats to Sahil Seth, Maki Potamianos, and Tony Xavier on the launch! [...] We just ran our own AI interview agent (Nora) on real candidates applying to our team.
Not a demo. Not a simulation. A real position, real applicants, real evaluation.
It's one thing to sell an AI hiring product. It's another to trust it with your own team. If you wouldn't use your own product to hire your next colleague, why would anyone else?
Here's what I've learned from using our own platform as our primary ATS: you find bugs that no QA process catches. You feel friction that no user report describes. And you build conviction that no pitch deck can fake.
Every feature request that comes from "I used this yesterday and it frustrated me" ships faster than any that comes from a roadmap spreadsheet. [...] Not every founder who's put off an AI hire is wrong to wait.
Some businesses genuinely don't need one yet, and the ones that do usually don't know it because "not sure if we need this" feels safer than finding out.
The real signal is whether the same manual task keeps costing you real hours, week after week, and you've caught yourself saying "we'll deal with that properly later" more than once, not how loud the hype is.
If neither describes you, an AI hire probably isn't the right move yet, and that's a fine place to land. If they do, the useful next step is a real conversation with someone who's mapped this decision for other founders before, not a job posting.
